negative_reviews.author: Shun
negative_reviews.text:
Cute staff but the food is absolutely disgusting
First time eating a bad vegan dish and by far the worst ramen I’ve ever tasted

negative_reviews.author: Paula. MzG
negative_reviews.text:
(Translated by Google) I had the vegan tofu ramen and was unfortunately a little disappointed, as it tasted rather bland and also looked different than in the pictures on the menu.

(Original)
Ich hatte das vegane Tofu Ramen und war leider ein bisschen enttäuscht, da es recht langweilig geschmeckt hat und auch anders aussah als auf den Bildern auf der Karte.

negative_reviews.author: Julia-Marie
negative_reviews.text:
(Translated by Google) All in all, it was okay since we got a table without a reservation, but we had to wait 30 minutes for our food. The broth was very tasty, as were the garnishes, although the meat was quite fatty and flabby. The service seemed unenthusiastic. The price-performance ratio wasn't really there. On top of that, I didn't think the 10% service charge was justified for the service provided.

(Original)
all in all wars schon gut, da wir ohne Reservierung einen Platz bekommen haben, aber wir mussten 30 Minuten auf unser Essen warten. Die Brühe war sehr lecker, die Einlagen auch, wobei das Fleisch schon sehr viel Fett/Wabbel hatte. Die Bedienung schien lustlos. Preis-Leistung nicht wirklich gegeben. Obendrauf die 10% Servicefee fand ich nicht gerechtfertigt für den Service.

negative_reviews.author: Lisa Collins
negative_reviews.text: Average food at a high price. It was okay, wouldn't come here again, have had better ramen elsewhere. Also added a sneaky service charge and don't tell you which I didn't appreciate.

issues: Steady weekday numbers, 34 more customers than last week; sales nearly 27,000 GBP, 9% above target.
Deliveroo login issue prevented data retrieval; Oisin advised contacting Junna.
Labour up slightly to 17.89% (tired team, extra weekend prep staff); food variance -4.2%, drinks 3.8%.
One star Google review from a first time customer who ordered the vegan tonkotsu.
Plan to hire part time FOH and BOH student workers for flexibility over the festival period.
Compliance 99%; extractor fan leak being fixed Saturday morning after quote approval.
Abby proposed redesigning the menu with spice levels in house specials instead of free chillies, estimated 4,000 to 5,000 GBP a year.
Region: food spend target temporarily raised to 26% until current promotions end (Matthew Jenner).
Region: hats or hairnets mandatory for all staff to prevent food contamination.
Region: GM and HC meeting notes must run through Google Meet so Gemini takes the notes; budget router templates updated, Monday dates must be entered correctly.
Spend per head dipped by £0.04 (0.18%) week on week.
Sales were £26,809.69, up £1,023.69 (3.96%) week on week and £2,309.69 (9.43%) above the £24,500 target; Abhi quoted about £28,000 to £29,000 on the BOH call, but the sheet figure is used.
Food cost was 23.42%.

Staff come in at staggered times and are stacked at busy periods, with one in the kitchen and one on the floor at quiet times, weekends focus on quick table turnarounds across about 40 seats over two floors, and much of the prep, such as pork belly, is done in house.

Hiring for a full time team member starts in November to cover two team members each taking a month's holiday in December and January, and Abhi prefers his own hire to sharing staff because Ikigai works very differently.
Broth should come from the factory and the supply chain is otherwise unchanged, so the site keeps ordering as before.
The BOH report shows no Google review feed for Ikigai 2 on the dashboard.
A building leak investigation is listed on the maintenance log.
The menus need reprinting because the current ones are in bad shape.

Region: five of the nine Scotland and Newcastle sites ran food cost above 25% (Maki 12, 1, 7, 3 and 8), which the Scotland BOH meeting of 13/10 linked to loyalty programme and delivery platform discounts across the group.

Region: new tonkotsu and chicken broth arrives from 15/10 and needs no added water; defrost it a day ahead and reheat it in a pot rather than straight on the heat, and a digital Brix meter is arriving to replace checking by eye, though not every site has one yet (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: new chicken arrives on 15/10 and the new char siu (different shape) and pre cooked frozen beef from 19/10, starting at Maki 8; defrost the beef a day ahead and grill or pan fry it for 15 seconds a side before slicing, holding extra stock because it cannot be used on the day it arrives (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: the frozen ramen promotion is postponed by one week, and Penny is checking with Michael whether frozen ramen counts in food cost or separately, as some sites have already bought it (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).
Spend per head held at £21.65 (AM Updates 14/10).
Abby has had no response from Marketing on promotional stamp cards over four weeks (AM Updates 14/10).
Teddy, Ka Ho and Michael held Abby up as the standard for GMs, as the site has grown without marketing help (AM Updates 14/10).

Region: Ka Ho put food cost of 25.3% to 27.2% at Maki 1, Fountainbridge, M7, M8 and M12 down to promotions lifting usage while sales projections were not adjusted; Michael said site leaders can ask for food cost and wage budget increases (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: a level 8 Halloween ramen with a super spicy factory chilli paste is launching with a video; one bag per site, about a teaspoon per bowl (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: snooze out of stock items on both Deliverect and the POS, or the whole delivery order fails (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: wage revenue baseline is 21% with up to 2% leeway; drinks cost moves to management, food cost to head chefs, new OKRs due end of November (AM Updates 14/10).
